insight: Psalm 27:1 and Hebrews 13:6 both express unwavering confidence in God's protective presence that dispels fear of human enemies. Psalm 27 emphasizes the LORD as light, salvation, and an impregnable fortress, leading David to ask rhetorically whom he should fear, while Hebrews echoes this assurance by declaring boldly that the Lord is the believer's personal helper, removing fear of what man can do. Both passages highlight faith grounded in God's covenantal help as the foundation for courage in the face of threats, transforming natural fear into confident trust.
